name: Verdant (Conduit Force of Nature)
body:
A connection to the verdant is a connection to the vegetative life of the world. They are suffused with the constantly growing power of plant life.

Manifestation: A connection to verdant will typically manifest as twigs and leaves among the conduit’s hair, the scent of flowers, the conduit’s blood may even take on a slightly thicker appearance like sap.

Communing: Communing with the verdant could be smelling flowers, tending a garden, sifting through dried herbs or watching the leaves of trees.

Connection Spells: (1st-level/0th) – germinate* (2nd-level/1st) – entangle (4th-level/2nd) – barkskin (6th-level/3rd) – thorny entanglement (8th-level/4th) – grove of respite (10th-level/5th) – wall of thorns (12th-level/6th) – fire seeds (14th-level/7th) – changestaff (16th-level/8th) – violent growth* (18th-level/9th) – shambler

Added Spells to Learn: Spells that mention plants, empower plants, summon plants, or allow transformation into plants.

Primal Empathy: The conduit may communicate with plant creatures as well as animals, magical beasts, fey and other creatures that live primarily in or on plant life at the GM’s discretion.

Natural Skill: Survival

Natural Movement: The conduit is not affected by any difficult terrain created by plants or other foliage.

Wooden Hands (Su)

Beginning with 1st level, so long as the conduit has 1 primal point remaining, they have a 1d6 slam attack as their hands are seemly made of hard wood.

Additionally, you can expend a primal point to have the damage dealt be considered magical and adamantine for damage reduction purposes. They also gain a +1 enhancement bonus to their natural armor. The bonus to natural armor increases by 1 at 5th level and every 5 levels thereafter.

Verdant Connection (Su)

At 5th level, as long as the conduit has at least 1 primal point remaining, they can detect the presence and location of any creature of the plant type as the spell detect animals or plants in a 60 ft. radius around the conduit. At 8th level, this ability extends to any creature in contact with plants.

Concentrating on this effect is a swift action each round.

Additionally, the conduit may expend a primal point as and take 10 minutes to cast commune with nature as a spell-like ability.

Plant Step (Sp)

At 9th level, the conduit can expend a primal point as a standard action, to teleport as per the spell dimension door as long as the beginning and ending points have plant life at least adjacent to the square. The caster level of this spell-like ability is equal to the conduit’s class level.

Verdant Dominion (Sp)

At 13th level, the conduit may spend a primal point to use the dominate monster spell with the force of nature’s DC. This ability only affects creatures of the plant and fey types. Fey gain a +5 bonus to their Will save against the effect. The HD of the affected creature may not exceed the conduit’s class levels. The conduit may only have one creature dominated in this way. They may release a dominated creature as a free action though the affected creature’s attitude is hostile upon its release. On a successful save, the creature is immediately hostile but has the shaken condition for 1d6 rounds even if they would normally be immune to such effects.

Lord of Plants (Su)

At 17th level, the conduit no longer needs to have primal points remaining for the ongoing effects of the wooden hands or verdant connection abilities and the radius of verdant connection extends to 120 ft. Additionally, their plant step can act like the tree stride spell.

Additionally, no creature of the plant types may attack the conduit unless magically compelled or attacked by the conduit first. In either case, they must make a Will save or be shaken while within 30 feet of the conduit if of indifferent or lower disposition. This shaken condition is applicable even if they are normally immune.

The following abilities are chosen when a conduit gains a primal ability. They are grouped into sections that tie into each other for ease of reference.
